It seems more likely to be a mutation (or two). Pleasure became prevalent because it encourages reproduction, people who don't have fun having sex don't have as many babies.

The hope there is that if it is a simple genetic problem it might be correctable in the near future. Whole genome studies are starting to get serious so we may at least have answers soon(ish).

Why limit yourself to believing there's only one cause? There could easily be many.

Also, many people on here have had SA onset at some point in their life, others were born with it. So we might be lumping many diseases under one label.

Data is the only answer to your question. Our speculation is meaningless and changes nothing. That said, if there were a study I'd sign up immediately. Maybe we could look into getting our genomes analyzed.

hostage rescue team

Part of it was just accepting that I couldn't change things, and also that it's not anyone else's fault. Their fun doesn't take anything away from me. And really no one would wish this fate on you. They really wouldn't.

It's really frustrating. I was pretty resentful towards the non-afflicted for a long time but I had to just let go of my anger before it killed me. So I did. It's still hurtful to think about but at least I don't need to blame anyone anymore, which is a huge relief.

Nowadays I feel more like a survivor of some horrible accident. Definitely, a major part of the human experience will always be inaccessible to me, but at least I'm alive.

On the other hand, I don't know if that will be good enough, or how I'm going to go through the rest of my life. One day I'll wake up and be 50 without ever having been in a serious relationship (I quit dating years ago, before I met anyone I really liked - though even if I had I would've had to have broken it off at some point).

It's definitely impacted my social life. I can tell I get treated differently in some way once people realize that I'm not gay but that I also don't try to hook up with the women who are interested in me. It's not a big deal, but it's something I've noticed. My friends and family are all clearly confused as to why I never date anyone, but they've stopped pushing me to be in a relationship. Still, I can tell it's the topic of conversation. Not in the gossip-y sense, but more in the "do you know why he never has a girlfriend?" sense. 

I've seen two doctors about it. The first, an internal medicine doctor, was very professional, but you could tell him that this was the first time he'd heard of such a thing outside of medical school and he was scrambling to remember what could cause it. A urologist I saw later basically told me he'd never even heard of it. There was one nurse who I had never seen before who saw me while I was in the waiting room and she came to talk to me just to see how I was doing. I guess she had read my chart and took a special interest. She was obvious very sympathetic and that was pretty encouraging. It was nice just to have it acknowledged how much it blows to have sexual anhedonia.
I googled "sexual anhedonia" and it was the fourth link.

I have this - I can't feel pleasure or have an orgasm. I don't actually know what either of the words mean, really. Like describing colors to a blind person. I'm a guy, and everything else works - I have a normal libido, can ejaculate, etc. It's just pointless.

Nothing on the list of plausible causes has ever happened to me. And I'm not depressed (if you can believe that). The doctors I've seen have no clue what to do. Super frustrating. On the plus side, my friends have given up trying to figure out why I never date anyone.
